newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers' strike enters second week.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers' strike enters second week.

text.p: Colombia's government on Monday said truck drivers were gradually returning to work but their union said the crippling strike was still in full force as it entered its second week.

The government declared the strike illegal on Friday and Transporation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez said drivers slowly began going back to work over the weekend to avert the threat of having their operators' licenses revoked. "The strike is being lifted gradually," Lopez told the Caracol radio station.

The Colombian Truck Drivers Association issued a statement saying the strike remained in full force and there had been no move to lift it. Private exporters confirmed that no shipments of coffee or other key commodities were being dispatched to ports and said export industries remained paralysed by the job action despite government efforts to halt it.
"There are no signs of relief," one exasperated coffee exporter said in a telephone interview.

The bulk exporter, who spoke on condition he not be identified, estimated that at least 250,000 132-pound (60-kg) bags of coffee that private exporters had promised clients for delivery in October would be delayed at least until November. Another 250,000 bags promised for delivery during the first half of November would be delayed until the second half of the month, he said.

The delays come amidst an extremely tight supply situation in consumer countries that could trigger panic by the first week of November if Colombia's strike continues, the exporter said. "The bottom line is that we're paralysed commercially," he said.
Spokesmen for the Colombian Exporters Association could not be reached for immediate comment.
Among other demands, striking drivers are holding out for a 30 percent hike in freight rates against government offers of a 15 percent increase.
